name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East. Colonial hill station at about 1,500 m elevation with pine forests, markets, lakes, and base for exploring waterfalls, caves, and living root bridges.
facts: State capital and HQ of East Khasi Hills
Elevation approximately 1,496 m
Named after the deity U Shyllong
Major educational and administrative hub of Northeast India

name: Jowai
description: Headquarters of West Jaintia Hills district and cultural centre of the Pnar (Jaintia) people. Hill town at about 1,380 m elevation surrounded by the Myntdu River, gateway to Nartiang, Thadlaskein, Krang Suri and the southern Umngot River circuit.
facts: HQ of West Jaintia Hills district
Elevation approximately 1,380 m
About 64 km from Shillong on NH6
Cultural hub for Behdeinkhlam festival and Pnar traditions

name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Iconic multi-tiered waterfall near Amlarem in West Jaintia Hills with a striking turquoise plunge pool. Popular for swimming (life jackets available), photography and short treks; one of Meghalaya’s most photographed nature spots.
facts: Located near Amlarem, about 30 km from Jowai
Famous for crystal-clear blue-green pool
Short 10–15 minute walk from parking
Entry fee applies; best October–April

name: Dawki / Umngot River
description: Border town on the India–Bangladesh frontier famous for the crystal-clear Umngot River where boats appear to float in mid-air. Historic 1932 British suspension bridge; major boating and photography destination.
facts: Umngot River considered one of India’s cleanest
Best clarity November–March
1932 suspension bridge over the river
Indo-Bangladesh border check post at Tamabil

name: Shnongpdeng Village
description: Riverside eco-tourism village a few kilometres upstream from Dawki on the Umngot River. Community-managed hub for camping, kayaking, cliff jumping and quieter boating away from the main border traffic.
facts: About 7–8 km upstream from Dawki
Community-managed adventure and camping site
Clearer and quieter stretches of Umngot River
Homestays and riverside tents available

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest concentration of megalithic stones in the Khasi-Jaintia region, north of Nartiang market. Menhirs and dolmens erected from the 16th–19th centuries by Jaintia chiefs and clans; often called the Stonehenge of Northeast India.
facts: About 24–30 km from Jowai
Largest collection of monoliths in Meghalaya
Tallest menhir erected by U Mar Phalyngki
Declared of national importance; free entry

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: 600-year-old Shakti Peeth dedicated to Goddess Jayanti (Durga) in Nartiang village. One of the 51 Shakti Peethas where Sati’s left thigh is believed to have fallen; major pilgrimage site especially during Durga Puja.
facts: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas
About 600 years old; summer capital of Jaintia kings
Dedicated to Jayanti and Kamadishwar
Within walking distance of Nartiang Monoliths

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Historic man-made lake (also Pung Sajar Nangli) beside NH6 near Mukhla village, about 8–10 km from Jowai. Legend says it was dug by the followers of U Sajar Nangli using only bow tips; popular picnic and boating spot.
facts: About 8–10 km from Jowai on NH6
Man-made according to local legend of Sajar Nangli
Fed by perennial spring
Popular for picnics and short boat rides

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Two-tiered secluded waterfall in the Amlarem area with a clear blue plunge pool. Accessed by a moderate trek; popular for swimming and quieter nature experiences away from main tourist circuits.
facts: Located in Amlarem sub-division
About 80 km from Shillong
Two-tiered falls with blue plunge pool
Moderate trek through forest

name: Thlu Muwi Stone Bridge
description: Ancient megalithic stone bridge over the Muwi stream, about 16 km from Jowai on the road toward Dawki. Built with massive granite slabs by Jaintia warriors under royal orders to facilitate travel between Nartiang and Jaintiapur; nearby waterfall.
facts: About 16 km from Jowai toward Dawki
Built by U Mar Phalyngki and U Luh Lamare
Massive granite slabs without mortar
Adjacent Muwi Waterfalls
